about: AGNT Protocol version 1 test vectors (spec/PROTOCOL.md section 15). Each section says what its cases mean. Private keys are 32-byte seeds in hex (RFC 8032 for Ed25519, FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen for ML-DSA-65); every other byte string is as it appears on the wire. ML-DSA-65 signatures are hedged, so another implementation verifies them rather than reproducing them.

keys.about: The keys every section uses, from their seeds. erin and frank are principals who pair with agents by key.

canonical.about: Canonical JSON (section 5.1): each input, parsed under the strict rules, has the canonical form given, or is refused for the reason given. inputHex is raw bytes.

cases.refused: a raw control character in a string

addresses.about: Addresses (section 2.1). wire: the version 1 wire form of the input from any case, or null. anyVersion: whether the input as written is an address a message of any version may carry: the invariant local part (1 to 64 bytes of UTF-8 with no @, no space, no ASCII capital and no character of category Cc), and a domain. Routers do not judge normalisation, so a local part not in NFC, or holding a mark assigned only in a recent Unicode version, is an address to every router.

timestamps.about: Timestamps (section 2.5): the instant each names in milliseconds since 1970 (negative before it), or null when it is not a wire timestamp.

keyTokens.about: Key tokens (section 2.3): whether each is a key of an algorithm version 1 defines. An algorithm a reader does not implement is never a key to it.

keyLists.about: Key lists as documents carry them (section 4), read at now: read is the entries a reader implementing both algorithms keeps, or null when the list makes the document unreadable. At most 32 total entries may be published, including retained revoked entries. An entry revoked more than 300 seconds after now makes the list unreadable.

messages.about: Signed messages (sections 1 and 5): signingBytes is AGNT-MESSAGE, a newline, and the canonical message without signature; id is the SHA-256 of those canonical bytes without the prefix; signer is the key that verifies the signature.

headerValues.about: The values of four headers the protocol names (section 5.4), and whether each is well formed: for, critical, pairing, and listed, whose only value is yes (placement is in messageChecks). A for header is a principal (section 2.2), written exactly, with nothing percent-encoded.

pairings.about: Pairings (sections 2.2 and 5.4): bytes is AGNT-PAIR, the agent address and the principal, joined by newlines; pairing is the principal key's signature, the value of the pairing header; verifies is whether it verifies for this agent and principal.

signatures.about: Signature verification (sections 2.3 and 2.4), over the signingBytes of the message named. keyValidAt: the verdict with the key entries given. refused: signatures every verifier refuses with the author key, though [S]B - [k]A = R holds as points or holds after multiplying by the cofactor. mixedOrder: verdicts with a key of mixed order, which must agree across verifiers.

requests.about: Signed requests (section 8). signed: requests, the eight-line signing string the server rebuilds (its fourth line is actor, the value of agnt-agent or agnt-server), and headers whose signature verifies with agnt-key. checks: what a server answers to each request at now, given the key entry it holds for agnt-key (null: none), whether it holds the nonce from this key (a server keeps a nonce until the timestamp of its request leaves the window), and whether it is a server request (server: agnt-server required) or an agent request (agent: agnt-agent required); request.actor is the identity line the server signs over. The refusals come in the order of section 8: headers, window, key, validity, signature, and only then the nonce. details are as the server sends them. nonces: until when a server keeps a nonce, given the agnt-timestamp of its request: the first moment that timestamp is outside the window, checked in whole seconds. addKeyProofs: the proof a new key signs (CLIENT.md, register). signedFor: the origin line a request to a server whose origin is written as given signs, the serialised origin (section 3); agnt-server carries the same form, and any other is refused. addressSegments: an address as one path segment: every byte that is not an RFC 3986 pchar percent-encoded with upper-case hex, @ literal; a server reads the target exactly as sent, before any decoding.

signals.about: Signals (section 6.4) posted to receiver from the server whose keys are serverKeys, at now. signingBytes is AGNT-SIGNAL, a newline, and the canonical signal without signature. Whether a signal reaches an agent is the receiving server's own policy; no vector fixes it.

resolution.about: Resolution (section 3) of domain (example.com when absent). txt is the TXT records at _agnt.<domain>, each as its character strings, or "servfail" or "dnssec_failure". wellKnown is the answer to GET https://<domain>/.well-known/agnt: a status and body, or how the fetch failed: "nxdomain", "refused" or "bad_certificate" (absences, so not_found), or "timeout" or "dropped" (temporary); when absent it must not be fetched. origins: server origins as written, and as compared. cacheMs: the longest a resolver may cache each outcome, given the lifetime its source allows (sourceTtlMs: the DNS TTL, or the HTTP freshness lifetime).
